details.summary: This is a remarkably well-designed recipe that captures the comforting essence of a chowder while strictly adhering to both fatty liver and type 2 diabetes guidelines. The use of smoked paprika to replace bacon and partial mashing to replace a roux are excellent culinary choices, making it a perfect fit for the book.

dimensions.feedback: The flavor profile is excellent; using smoked paprika is a very smart, liver-friendly way to mimic the traditional bacon flavor in a chowder without the saturated fat and sodium.
All ingredients are correctly listed and integrated seamlessly into the instructions.

Instructions are comprehensive and well-paced. Time ranges are provided, a 10-minute doneness check is explicitly stated for the potatoes, and the warning not to boil the milk at the end is an essential, appreciated touch.
Fits the New England chowder inspiration perfectly while elegantly adapting the traditional heavy fats for the dietary guidelines.
Stovetop simmering and partial mashing directly in the pot is the ideal technique to thicken a dairy-light chowder without resorting to a refined-flour roux.

Nutrition calculation is highly plausible. The automated check correctly flagged the total carbohydrate at 47.1g (just over the 45g ceiling), but because the source is entirely unrefined complex starches (potatoes and corn) alongside high protein and fiber, it does not harm the recipe. If strict numerical compliance is desired, reducing the frozen sweet corn to 5.3 oz (150 g) will perfectly land it inside the 35-45g window.
Title and intro accurately describe the dish and set realistic, appealing expectations without any banned health claims or overly clinical language.
Highly appealing. It is a comforting, satisfying, fast meal that feels rich and indulgent without using heavy cream or excessive butter.
Perfectly balances liver health (omega-3 fatty acids, low saturated fat) and blood sugar management (high protein, substantial fiber, whole-food carbohydrates).
Outstanding. There are zero added sugars, and the carbohydrates come purely from whole-food sources (potatoes, sweet corn) and the natural lactose in the milk.
Fits the 'light_main' Soups & Salads chapter perfectly as a complete, substantial bowl that carries its own high-quality protein and complex carbohydrates.
Prep is minimal and utilizes incredibly practical pantry/freezer staples (frozen corn, canned salmon). A home cook will easily finish this well within the 30-minute window.
